extracted.intended_audience: SNSF staff, programme evaluators, policymakers, prospective Ambizione applicants and host institutions
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of evaluation criteria and procedural/eligibility standards used in the SNSF Ambizione programme final evaluation report (eligibility rules, evaluation procedure, evaluation questions, survey metrics, implementation/impact dimensions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal eligibility requirements for Ambizione applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant applicants must meet a number of personal requirements to be eligible for funding through Ambizione.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must hold a doctorate (PhD) obtained generally up to five years prior to submission; MD holders must have completed at least three years of post‑graduate clinical/practical work and may generally submit up to nine years after obtaining the medical licence; applicants must furnish proof of high‑level publications; applicants must have completed postdoctoral research activities lasting at least 12 months at a university other than the university that conferred the doctorate. (See: 'Regulations concerning Ambizione, Ambizione‑PROSPER and Ambizione‑SCORE grants', NRC version 13.08.2013.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑phase evaluation procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The evaluation procedure of Ambizione applications is organised in two phases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase 1: the National Research Council (NRC) of the SNSF makes an initial selection based on the documents submitted. Phase 2: applications are peer‑reviewed and candidates are invited to an interview to present their research project and career plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concept of the Ambizione funding scheme (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the goals, design and target groups of Ambizione are suitable and coherent, and whether Ambizione is harmonised with other SNSF funding instruments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific evaluation questions: Are the goals, the design (extent of the grant, funding criteria and requirements, additional support, etc.) and the target groups of Ambizione suitable? Is Ambizione harmonised with other (similar) funding instruments of the SNSF? The evaluation looked at coherence, adequacy across diverse fields, the role of international mobility, and whether individual case assessment is feasible under regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of Ambizione by SNSF and host institutions (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how the SNSF and host institutions implement Ambizione with respect to support and integration of grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key questions: Is the support that the SNSF offers Ambizione grantees sufficient? Are grantees supported adequately by the host institutions? How are collaboration between hosts and grantees and the integration of the grantees into the host institutions evaluated? The evaluation considers SNSF advisory support, case‑by‑case interpretation of rules, and common problems (e.g. misclassification of grantees as regular postdocs or excessive teaching loads).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach of the Ambizione funding scheme (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether Ambizione reaches its defined target groups and whether it satisfies their needs and requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific evaluation questions: Are the target groups defined in the Ambizione funding scheme concept reached? Does Ambizione satisfy the needs and requirements of the target groups? The evaluation used SNSF application database distributions and surveys to assess representation of returning, incoming and limited mobility groups and female grantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Ambizione funding on grantees (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the effects of Ambizione funding on grantees' research independence, project completion, scientific profile, and career progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific evaluation questions: Have Ambizione grantees been able to carry out their research projects more independently? Were their projects successfully completed? Has the Ambizione grant enhanced the scientific profile of grantees (publications, awards, conference participation, further research)? Have grantees successfully carried on with their scientific careers (tenure track, professorship, group leader), and to what extent has Ambizione contributed? Are Ambizione grantees more successful than comparable unfunded researchers?

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact of Ambizione on host institutions (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate benefits and integration challenges experienced by host institutions from hiring Ambizione grantees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions include: In what ways do host institutions benefit (scientific exchange, boost to scientific performance)? Did hosts encounter difficulties integrating grantees into ongoing research and teaching? The evaluation examined co‑funding, infrastructure acquisition, and post‑grant employment patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overarching goals of Ambizione (evaluation objective)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether Ambizione meets its broader strategic goals related to national research capacity and diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation questions: Has Ambizione generated knowledge transfer into Switzerland? Has Ambizione helped researchers from Switzerland doing research abroad return to the Swiss scientific community? Is Ambizione an attractive funding scheme for young talents from abroad? Has Ambizione had specific effects in terms of gender?

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee satisfaction with submission and grant characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey metrics asking grantees how satisfied they are with administrative effort, submission requirements, amount and duration of the awarded Ambizione grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items reported: satisfaction with submission requirements, administrative effort involved in the application, amount of the awarded Ambizione grant, and duration of the awarded Ambizione grant. Results: very high satisfaction for submission/admin/amount; duration showed the highest share of dissatisfied respondents. (Figure 1 summaries and percentages provided in report.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction with SNSF information/advice and support
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure grantee satisfaction with information/advice provided by SNSF during application and with support/advice during the funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey items: '...the information/advice from the SNSF during the application process?' and '...the support/advice from the SNSF during the funding period?' Results: very high satisfaction (e.g., 96% very or rather satisfied during application; 65% very and 29% rather satisfied during funding period).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction with host institution implementation (infrastructure, support, integration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey metrics on grantees' satisfaction with the infrastructure at the host institute, support provided by the host institute, and integration into the host institute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Survey results: infrastructure satisfaction ~97%; support provided by host ~88% satisfied; integration ~85% satisfied. Host survey: 94% of hosts rated integration as good. Report examines dissatisfaction clusters (e.g., earlier cohorts, institution types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific forms of host support (types of support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Items capturing how host institutions supported grantees (use of infrastructure, additional financial support, acquisition of new infrastructure, support for activities like teaching).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 4 responses: use of existing infrastructures (96%); additional financial support for own research (34%); host financially supported acquisition of new infrastructure (28%); further/other support (18%); additional support for activities at the host (15%). Multiple responses possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and funding of scientific and other personnel support
rubrics_metrics.description: Metrics on whether grantees had access to doctoral students, postdocs and other personnel and how these were funded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Table 5: doctoral students available to 58% of respondents, postdocs 21%, other personnel 53%. Funding rules: postdocs must be funded at least 50% by the host institute. Table 6 provides breakdowns of funding sources (host, Ambizione grant, shared arrangements) for doctoral students, postdocs and other personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching activity participation and financing
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether grantees engaged in teaching, at what levels, hours per week, and how teaching activities were financed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 66% engaged in teaching; most taught 1–4 hours/week per semester. Table 7: teaching levels—Bachelor (61%), Master (71%), Doctoral (28%). Table 8: financing—fully funded through Ambizione grant (47%), partially Ambizione/host (11%), fully host (19%), other/don't know percentages reported.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticisms and suggested changes to scheme design (expert feedback)
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical evaluation points raised by experts about Ambizione's design and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key criticisms: three‑year funding period seen as too short (suggestion to extend to four years; implications for grant sum and success rates discussed); international mobility requirement criticised or seen as needing redefinition (holistic concept or broader career window); suggestion to allow parallel funding through Ambizione and other SNSF schemes; some experts argued grant sum is too low and suggested doubling amounts and covering salaries and equipment. Experts agreed success rate should not drop below 20%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case study selection and representativeness criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria used to select the 10 case studies of former Ambizione grantees for qualitative interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews chosen to match distribution of field of support (discipline), gender, and category (incoming/returning) of the complete sample of Ambizione grantees. Case study portraits were used to reflect personal and scientific backgrounds in detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey sampling and comparison group design
rubrics_metrics.description: Design choices for the online surveys to quantify views of target groups and allow comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First online survey addressed all Ambizione grantees 2008–2013 (complete sample) with two comparison groups: (1) persons with rejected Ambizione applications 2008–2013, and (2) persons with SNSF project funding as responsible applicant 2008–2013 (matched by being first‑time beneficiaries, age caps, and no prior Ambizione applications). Approximately 1,450 persons contacted; second survey addressed 257 contact persons at Ambizione host institutions. Surveys were open for two weeks with one reminder after one week.
